roster.name: Starhopper
roster.note: a single-engine test article hops 150 metres and lands — the first flight of the program, proving the basic control

roster.name: SN15 lands
roster.note: after a run of spectacular explosions, a Starship upper stage flies high and lands intact — the fly-fail-fix method applied to the biggest rocket ever built

roster.name: First integrated flight
roster.note: the full stack — Super Heavy booster and Starship — launches together for the first time; it clears the pad and is lost minutes later, and the data feeds the next attempt

roster.name: Booster catch
roster.note: the Super Heavy booster flies back and is caught out of the air by the launch tower's arms — a landing method no one had ever attempted at this scale
the uncrewed demonstration flights on the road to orbit, the Moon, and Mars
the intended end state — crewed Starships carrying people to the surface of Mars
